title: Per-tenant KMS affinity, audit-anchoring middleware, and RBACv2 scoped role templates
author: Asha Mehta
release_notes: Adds opt-in per-tenant KMS affinity routing, an audit-anchoring middleware that attaches HMAC-backed proof headers for forensic integrity, and RBACv2 scoped role templates to enforce tenant/region constraints. Feature gated; defaults are backward compatible.
description: Context and motivation: Customers in regulated regions asked for stronger, tenant-scoped guarantees tying KMS usage and audit traces to a tenant's residency preferences. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: (1) a per-tenant KMS affinity layer that prefers tenant-bound CMKs or region-preferred providers when available; (2) audit-anchoring middleware that produces a lightweight HMAC proof over request metadata and KV cache roots and appends an X-Audit-Proof header to the audit pipeline; (3) RBACv2 scoped role templates that generate tenant- and region-bound operator roles to reduce horizontal privilege. Design notes: the implementation is feature-flagged behind enableTenantKMSAffinity and enableAuditAnchor and is a non-breaking opt-in change. When enabled the affinity algorithm consults tenant metadata (tenant.claimed_region, tenant.kms_preference) and consults the KMS provider registry to pick a best-fit CMK; if no local match is resolvable we fall back to the global CMK and mark the audit proof with 'fallback' so downstream compliance tooling can triage. The audit-anchoring step is intentionally small (HMAC-SHA256 over request id, timestamp, tenant id, kms-key-id, and a short audit digest) so it can be validated by the audit consumer without needing full key material. Migration and rollout: default behavior remains unchanged until flags are enabled. Rollout plan: staged rollout to Dedicated cohort -> Canary in hosted -> broad enable; monitor kinesis audit_stream for proof acceptance rates and KMS error rate metrics. Security review: threat model and design doc attached; SEC-128 completed review with no blocking findings. Testing: unit tests for affinity selection, property-based tests for fallback behavior, and integration tests using the local KMS shim (localstack-compatible). Docs: admin docs and helm toggle entries added under docs/security/per-tenant-kms.md and helm values. Related: Linear ENG-4921, support ticket SUP-6041. Checklist: - [x] design doc and threat model linked - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] feature flags and helm values - [x] security review completed - [x] migration notes and docs
